description: Engineering handoff readiness policy. The Handoff gate answers 'is this contract complete enough for a developer to start, integrate, and demo?'. It introduces no new human approval: it reuses the existing Design Ready approval and checks only what the artifacts themselves declare.

authority.note: A semantic review recorded in HANDOFF-REVIEW.json is candidate evidence produced by a reviewer (often an AI). It never substitutes for a human approval row in PROJECT.md.

closure_policy.$comment: Who is allowed to say a finding is no longer open. Enforced by HANDOFF-010, not by prompt: an instruction an agent can ignore is not a control.
closure_policy.note: Any status other than open is a claim that someone decided something. That claim needs a resolvable decision reference. Accepting a risk or deferring work is a human judgement in every mode; an AI reviewer may additionally never close a finding under a human-only lens, whatever the decision reference says.
closure_policy.attestation_note: reviewer_kind is a self-declaration. No offline validator can prove who typed a JSON field, and pretending otherwise would be the same false assurance this framework exists to prevent. What IS enforced: a finding closed under a human-only lens must cite a DEC-### that exists in decision-log.md with a named decider. That makes the closure traceable to a governed artifact a person is accountable for, rather than to a word in a file.

freshness.note: Two digests, because a review can go stale two different ways. source_snapshot covers the material the requirements came from; review_inputs covers the governed artifacts the reviewer actually read. Changing BUILD-SPEC after a review leaves the source snapshot untouched, and without the second digest that review would still report as current.
freshness.review_input_note: Files absent from a project are skipped, and their absence is itself part of the digest. HANDOFF-REVIEW.json is deliberately excluded: a review cannot invalidate itself by being written.

lenses.title: Does the scope slice deliver the value the target milestone must show?
Is each declared capability complete across its lifecycle, not just the happy path?
Do entities, cardinality, quantities, and units support the declared use cases?
Does every state machine declare guards, terminal states, and reversal?
Are concurrent writes, retries, and unique-id allocation specified?
Can the declared build sequence actually be executed in that order?
Does every stream have a named owner, an integrator, and stated capacity?
Can each acceptance case be reached from the declared seed data?
Is each acceptance case classified as automated or manual, with a runner?
Do declared data elements, files, and free text have classification decisions?
Does the serving model satisfy the declared device and runtime capabilities?
Is there a declared startup, reset, degraded, and recovery path for the demo?

visual_proof.$comment: Milestone 10. This is a conditional evidence check within Handoff, not a new approval or a requirement to create design artifacts. It activates only when a project already has the full creative-direction/design-system trio declared below.

rubric.title: The visible choices fit the selected direction and brief.
The result avoids an unexamined generic default.
Typography has an intentional, legible hierarchy.
The first read and action priority are clear.
Composition and density serve the product task.
Components share a coherent visual grammar.
The scoped screens stay coherent together.
Visible states and recorded gaps are honest.
Desktop and mobile captures fit their declared viewports.
Legibility, contrast, and state communication were considered.
Sample content supports the intended review without misrepresenting source data.
A developer can trace the sheet to the documented contract.
No unscoped screen or capability is implied by the presentation.

freshness.note: The proof file does not hash itself. Every source-facing creative artifact, brand asset, and committed desktop/mobile capture participates, so an edit after review makes the evidence stale. This proves current file identity, not pixel provenance or visual quality.

authority.note: An AI may draft a candidate record, but the completed review needs a named human reviewer and a resolvable project DEC-### with a named decision owner. reviewer_kind is an attestation, not proof of identity.

owner_policy.note: A generic token is not a name. HANDOFF-003 checks only whether the declared owner is one of these tokens or blank; it never checks whether a named person is the *right* person.

not_required_policy.note: A section may be declared not_required only when the policy below allows it for that mode AND a rationale is written. Leaving a section body blank is never acceptable.

table_headers.$comment: HANDOFF-013. The validator reads table cells by column name, so a renamed or reordered header does not raise an error -- it silently yields empty cells, and the failure surfaces as some downstream rule complaining about a value the author did in fact fill in. Asserting the header turns that into one accurate diagnostic.
table_headers.order_note: Order is part of the contract because the columns are declared as an ordered list and a reader scanning two projects should find the same shape in both. A reordered header is reported separately from a renamed one.
table_headers.scope_note: Only tables whose columns are declared in this file. Column *counts* in templates are already covered by TABLE-001; this is about names and order in project artifacts.

project_identity.$comment: HANDOFF-014. PROJECT.md's own heading is the project's declaration of identity; the handoff artifacts have to agree with it. The exposure is a project started by copying another: HANDOFF.md keeps the old code, every other check passes, and the sheet names a project that is not the one being validated.
project_identity.authority_note: The heading, not the directory name: a project can legitimately live in a differently named folder, so the folder is the weaker source.

sensitive_data.note: The validator never infers sensitivity from a domain word. It reads the 'Contains Sensitive Data' column the author wrote. If that column says yes, a Classification Decision reference must exist.
sensitive_data.undeclared_note: A value that is neither a yes nor a no -- blank, 'maybe', 'unclear', 'probably not' -- is an undeclared classification, not a negative one. Treating it as no let a row opt out of HANDOFF-011 by being vague, which is the opposite of what a data inventory is for. The author must decide; the validator still never decides for them.

environment_capabilities.note: The validator never infers that a capability needs HTTPS or a camera. It reads the declared Capability rows and checks that each one has a resolved Serving Model and Environment Decision.

open_finding_penalty.$comment: Points deducted from a dimension for each OPEN review finding whose lens belongs to it. A finding that a reader raised and nobody closed is missing evidence, and the score has to show that even when no deterministic rule fired -- otherwise a project reads 100/100 while its own review says the demo will not work.

open_action_penalty.$comment: Points deducted per OPEN row in HANDOFF.md Open Actions, charged to the dimension its blocking point belongs to. Without this a project could block its own demo and still score 100/100 -- a number that contradicts the verdict printed above it is worse than no number.

caps.when: no named owner or no build sequence
an open critical finding blocks before_build

score.disclaimer: A readiness score summarizes declared evidence. It is not an approval, it does not transfer accountability, and no gate may be passed on the strength of a score alone.
